intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: stack frame — An entry containing the state for one active function call.
unwind — Return from calls in reverse order after a base case is reached.
local variable — A variable owned by a particular invocation.
call stack — Last-in, first-out storage for active calls.
base case — A condition that ends recursion.

blocks.title: Build the stack
blocks.text: SumTo(4) waits for SumTo(3), which waits for SumTo(2), which waits for SumTo(1).

blocks.title: Separate the local values
blocks.text: Each stack frame holds its own n: 4, 3, 2 or 1. The values do not overwrite one another.

blocks.title: Unwind from the top
blocks.text: SumTo(1) returns 1; SumTo(2) returns 3; SumTo(3) returns 6; SumTo(4) returns 10.

blocks.title: Worked example · Draw the call-stack frames for SumTo(3). Which call returns first?
Worked example · Push
blocks.text: The frames are SumTo(3), SumTo(2), then SumTo(1), with SumTo(1) at the top.

questions.prompt: Choose the response that best addresses this independent task: Foundation · QUESTION 1 OF 3 List the call-stack frames from bottom to top for SumTo(4).
questions.answer: SumTo(4), SumTo(3), SumTo(2), SumTo(1). SumTo(1) is the top frame.
options: The expression describes the final arithmetic but not execution order. The deepest call SumTo(1) must return first; only then can waiting calls compute their sums.
